subject: Food Science
title: Sugar Industry Cover-Up
description: A quick win: understand Sugar Industry Cover-Up.

hook.text: In 2016, JAMA Internal Medicine published evidence that the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists in the 1960s to blame fat.

buildup.text: The Sugar Research Foundation funded studies in 1967 that minimized sugar's role in heart disease and blamed dietary fat.

discovery.text: Internal documents showed the SRF paid three Harvard scientists $50,000 (today's equivalent: $400,000) to produce a review.

twist.text: The resulting low-fat dietary guidelines (1980–2010) led to 30 years of increased sugar consumption, obesity, and metabolic.

climax.text: The conflict-of-interest rules that exist today in nutrition science—mandatory disclosure, funding transparency.

punchline.text: Paid science, wrong guidelines, 30 years of damage. One industry's deception shaped.

quiz.question: What did the sugar industry fund Harvard scientists to do in the 1960s?
options: Produce research that shifted blame for heart disease from sugar to saturated fat
